title: Even conjectural certainty excludes doubt proper, which suspends judgment
source_text: VII. Caeterum ex Scholae Romanae sententia, certitudo quaelibet etiam conjecturalis, quae infimum obtinet gradum, excludit dubitationem, & illi opponitur. Nec enim ullo modo certus de aliqua re dici potest qui de ea dubitat. Nam qui proprie loquendo dubitat neutri parti contradictionis assentiri audet, & inter utramque judicium suspendit. Qui vero certus est, quamvis conjecturaliter tantum, alteri parti tamen assentitur, & determinate judicat rem ita se habere.
pass_a_gloss: But according to the mind of the Roman School, any certainty, even conjectural, which holds the lowest degree, excludes doubt and is opposed to it. For in no way can one be called certain of something who doubts of it. For he who properly speaking doubts dares assent to neither side of the contradiction and suspends judgment between both. But he who is certain, even if only conjecturally, nevertheless assents to one side and determinately judges that the matter is so.
pass_b_english: For Romans even the lowest certainty still excludes doubt proper.
Doubt suspends assent; certainty, even conjectural, determinately takes one side.
